column1: # Which package owns which check.
# Format: check<TAB>owner[<TAB>shards]
# `shards`, when present, splits one check across that many jobs (#262): a
# check past the wall-clock budget on its own is split by a declared count
# here, never by dropping a member or a check. A sharded check is its
# package's only check, and scripts/check-ci-coverage.py proves its shards
# complete -- every member in exactly one -- and refuses any package whose
# measured seconds (.github/check-seconds.tsv) per shard pass the budget.
# `verify.sh` defines what a check IS; this table decides where CI runs it.
# One source of truth: each per-package workflow derives its check list from
# here rather than naming checks itself, so the two cannot drift.
# scripts/check-ci-coverage.py requires every check `verify.sh --list` names to
# have exactly one owner here, and every owner to have a workflow that the root
# workflow calls and the gate job depends on. A check owned by nobody would run
# nowhere while CI still went green.
# A package with no checks simply has no row and no workflow: a workflow that
# runs nothing is a vacuous pass.
# --- diet: the Rust crate, and the formats it owns ---
fmt
clippy
test
library
regimen
lanes
# --- results: the claim-with-evidence invariant. Owned by diet since the
# record's format verdict comes from `diet check-record`, and a job without
# the toolchain could not build the binary it dispatches to. ---
results
# --- recompute: gate 0. Owned by diet for the same reason results is: the
# linter it sits beside dispatches the record verdict to the built binary. ---
admission
# --- pages: the published static surface. pages/ and
# .github/workflows/pages.yml -- the landing page and the deploy that
# publishes the replay and the ledger beside it -- are track five's (#32,
# ruling 8); the checks that guard them stay track one's. ---
pages
# --- repo: concerns that belong to no single package ---
hygiene
metadata
ci
history
resolver
derive
parity
# --- bsd: the injections applied again under a BSD-shaped sed (#75). Its own
# package, so its own job beside repo's, because applying every injection twice
# in one job is past the wall-clock budget (#260, ruled 2026-10-02). ---
bsd
# --- injections and recompute: each past the budget on its own, so each is
# a package of its own, split by name (#262). No recompute.sh runs `diet`
# (#268's review), so recompute's job needs no toolchain. ---
injections
recompute
# --- exercise: the web surface. Its own job, because it is the one package
# that needs Node, pnpm and a browser rather than the Rust toolchain. ---
exercise
